reason: The EM and the CTO merge into a develop branch without a merge decision card. This roster exists so that rule is a reviewable artifact instead of a convention buried in a prompt. No role attests a review: the review gate is the board's own review pass that left its findings on the PR, with those comments resolved or addressed (Chris, 2026-10-15). QA is not in the review path, and a `qa/gate` status is ignored (Chris, 2026-10-17).

merge_authorities.title: CTO
merge_authorities.note: Merge authority for develop. Also the escalation target when the queue itself is wrong.

merge_authorities.title: Engineering Manager
merge_authorities.note: Merge authority for develop. Owns queue order and hands a blocked PR back with a reason.

blocked_bases_reason: Mirrors the AGENTS.md 'Still stop and ask' gate: a merge into a release or trunk branch is a human decision. The queue refuses these outright rather than asking a caller to pass a flag.

defaults.required_checks_note: Fallback for any repo with no entry in required_checks_by_repo. No current repo relies on it: digithings-ai/digithings is named explicitly (DIG-690) and digithings-ai/twelve-x is named explicitly (DIG-4454).
defaults.ignored_checks_note: Check names the queue must not read as a blocker, because they are not required: either their verdict cannot be trusted, or the queue's own gates already decide the question. The list is global: every repository the queue manages is read against the same list, so an ignored name is skipped in the scan for red non-required checks. It is skipped there only. A name that is ALSO required - by required_checks_by_repo, or by the defaults.required_checks fallback - is still enforced by the required loop, and ignoring it does not discharge that obligation. The value must be a JSON array of names, not a string: a bare string is iterated character by character. `test` and `pricing-parity` are twelve-x's GitHub Actions jobs, which cannot start at all while the org's Actions billing is blocked (DIG-4454): every pull request reports them FAILURE with no log and no work done, so every pull request would be refused no matter what the local mirror says. They are listed for every repository, not only twelve-x, because the list is global; digithings reports no job by either name today. The local mirror `~/Code/local-ci/twelvex_ci.py` runs the equivalent work (ruff, deno test, pytest) and posts `local-ci`, which is the required check. `review-applied` is a commit status the local worker posts. It used to be untrustworthy because its failure row could be OLDER than the review comment it complains about: the dispatcher never re-runs a pull request whose `local-ci` row is already terminal, so a review that landed after the check left a failure behind that nothing ever refreshed. The dispatcher now re-runs a pull request whose failing `review-applied` row predates an in-session review comment (digiforge `6825d51`, 2026-10-21), so a failure that a review already cleared is refreshed; a review landing between the worker's comment read and its status post is not caught until the next review. It stays ignored anyway, because the queue decides review coverage itself: it accepts the `reviewed:agent` label together with an `<!-- in-session-review -->` comment, a completed reviewer bot or a `Cursor Bugbot` check that concluded success, a non-bot approval, or `reviewed:owner`, and it refuses a pull request whose review decision is CHANGES_REQUESTED or whose review threads are unresolved. Keeping the status out of the blockers leaves that gate as the single authority on a merge, with one deliberate difference: the queue accepts an outdated thread as resolved, where `review-applied` additionally wanted a fix commit and a reply on that thread. Remove `test` and `pricing-parity` when Actions billing is restored and the twelve-x entry in required_checks_by_repo goes back to `test`.

required_checks_by_repo_note:
The digithings entry matches the repo's own branch protection on `develop`, read from GET /repos/digithings-ai/digithings/branches/develop/protection/required_status_checks (strict: true), which requires exactly `local-ci` (DIG-3707, 2026-10-15). The three GitHub Actions names (`Required checks passed`, `doc-links + agents-init`, `mypy — digibase + digikey`) were retired with them: Actions minutes are exhausted and PR workflows are switched off (DIG-3604), so no new PR head ever reports them. They were chosen to match GitHub rather than ci.yml’s job names, so the queue cannot approve something GitHub would refuse.

The twelve-x entry is a deliberate TEMPORARY divergence from the repo's own CI. Twelve-x's required check was the GitHub Actions job `test`; from 2026-10-19 that job cannot start at all because the org's Actions billing is blocked ("recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased", DIG-4454), so every PR reports `required check 'test' is FAILURE` and nothing can merge until the monthly minutes reset. The host mirror `~/Code/local-ci/twelvex_ci.py` runs the same work locally (ruff, deno test, pytest, and a report-only pricing parity) and posts a `local-ci` commit status, so the queue requires that instead. Revert this entry to `test` when Actions billing is restored; do not leave it in place because a local mirror is cheaper — the point of naming it is that a reader can tell which machine produced the verdict.
ci_provenance_note: The provenance gate asks a `local-ci` status to name the build that made it green, and then reads that build back from the Woodpecker API (DIG-4794). A commit status is worth only what its writer is worth - GitHub's own words: any person or integration with write permissions can set the state of any status check - and both repositories name `local-ci` as their required check, so without this the queue would merge on a green word written by anyone with a token. The gate refuses a status whose `target_url` is missing, is not absolute, names a host that is not ours, is not a Woodpecker pipeline link, names another Woodpecker repository, names a build that is not there, names a build in which this repository's own check step did not succeed, or names a build that ran another commit. Every refusal says which of those it was. `mode` is one of `off`, `shadow` and `enforce`, and the environment variable MQ_CI_PROVENANCE overrides the file, so the mode can be changed on the running host without a code change; a value that is not one of the three names is treated as `enforce`, because a misspelled switch must not silence a gate. A `ci_provenance` block with no `mode` means `shadow`, and no `ci_provenance` block at all means `off`, so an older policy file stays loadable; a `mode` in the file that is not one of the three names is a different case, because the file is read once per tick, so it aborts the tick loudly and puts the traceback in the job's error log. The gate is keyed off `status_context_checks` by name, the same way the exemption above is, so any future repository that requires a check literally named `local-ci` inherits this gate too and is refused until it is added to `woodpecker_repos` and `steps`. The mode is `shadow` because the build that runs the check today is the launcher pipeline, and Woodpecker binds a pipeline to the commit its own repository checked out - the launcher's `main` commit, never the pull request head - so the commit comparison refuses every pull request. Shadow records what it would have refused, in the launchd job's error log and in ~/.config/digithings/merge-queue/ci-provenance.log, and merges anyway. The log holds one line per refusal and not one line per refusal per tick: the queue reads every open pull request on every tick, so writing the line again each time is how the 48 hour window turns into tens of thousands of lines. A refusal that repeats is counted in the index beside the log (~/.config/digithings/merge-queue/ci-provenance.index.json) instead, and the count says how often the gate saw it. DIG-4809 owns the 48 hour window and the switch to `enforce`, which happens only when the CI runs one build per pull request head. `hosts` is the part of the allow-list that never changes: it holds the loopback addresses only, because the deployment's own address is a DHCP address and a list that carries it goes stale - a stale list under `enforce` refuses every pull request, because every build link then names a host that is not ours. The deployment's addresses are read instead, from the files `host_files` names, taking the host and port of the URLs whose keys `host_url_keys` names; `require_config` says that the gate refuses when that configuration cannot be read, so a deployment that moved cannot be answered with a list that did not move with it. `token_file` is read for the WOODPECKER_TOKEN key only, and the value is never logged; the launchd job's environment carries no token, so the file is where the queue finds it. `woodpecker_repo_names` maps a GitHub repository to the Woodpecker repository that runs its check, named as `owner/name`; the numeric id is resolved from that name against the Woodpecker API at check time, because a repository that was recreated carries a new id and a number written down here would then point at a different repository. The name is the authority: when the lookup cannot be answered the gate refuses, and the number in the policy is not used in its place, because a number that cannot be confirmed names a repository the gate does not know and the build of an unknown repository says nothing about this pull request. The lookup adds no new way for the tick to fail, because the build behind the status is read from the same API. `woodpecker_repos` holds the number for a policy that names no repository by name, where there is nothing to resolve, and `woodpecker_names` gives the same `owner/name` for links that name the repository by name. `steps` names the step inside the build that answers for the repository - the launcher pipeline runs the digithings check and the twelve-x check side by side, so the pipeline on its own says nothing about which repository it answered for.
status_context_checks_note: Names accepted as commit statuses instead of workflow runs. `local-ci` is posted as a StatusContext by the local-ci daemon; no workflow ever reports a CheckRun by that name, so the CheckRun-evidence rule in merge_queue._gate_checks would refuse every PR if it applied. The exception is per-name: any other required check still needs a CheckRun. The list is per-name, not per-repo, so any future repo requiring a check literally named `local-ci` inherits the exemption: keep it to the names a repo's own gate actually produces. `digithings` names `local-ci` in its branch protection; `twelve-x` does not - since 2026-10-19 it is listed there because its Actions job `test` cannot start while billing is blocked (DIG-4454), and the cost is that a write token can post that status on a repo whose queue is the only gate. The `ci_provenance` block below is what pays that cost back: it asks the status to name the build it came from.
github_identity_note: Both authorities merge with the same org credential, so GitHub sees one committer. The role is an assertion the runner records in its audit comment, and an identity GitHub cannot enforce. So a role cannot stand behind a review either: `--attest-review` was removed on 2026-10-17 because the launchd wrapper hardcoded `qa` as the attesting role and nothing connected it to a QA act. Review evidence is now an artifact on the PR (see merge_queue._review_coverage), and merge_queue.py refuses any role that is not on this roster. Treat editing this file to add a role as a policy change that needs the CEO, not a routine edit. The reviewer-independence block above is the same problem seen from the other side: one GitHub login means GitHub cannot say which seat wrote a review, so the seat identity travels inside the review artifact and the queue checks it against the Paperclip side.

review_independence.mode_note: How the queue treats a review marker that may come from the PR author's own seat (DIG-4795). `off` reads no provenance at all, `shadow` measures what the gate would refuse and merges anyway, `enforce` refuses. The env var `MQ_REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE` overrides this file, and a value that is not one of the three is read as `enforce`: a misspelled switch must never turn a security gate off. The file says `shadow` because DIG-4809 named the two-step rollout — 48 hours of shadow so the queue can report what it would refuse, then a separate small PR that flips this to `enforce`. Enforce cannot come first: no review marker carries its seat and head yet, so enforce today would refuse every open PR.
review_independence.api_url_note: The Paperclip API the gate reads tickets, seats and runs from. It is the same local server the seats talk to. The queue runs from launchd with no Paperclip credential in its environment, so the key comes from the macOS keychain: the same `digithings` / `paperclip-api-key` item `kit/bin/dt-paperclip-key` manages and the same one `com.digithings.decide-poll.plist` exports. The key is a header value and nothing else — it is never printed, logged or written anywhere.
review_independence.log_path_note: Where shadow mode writes what it would have refused. The file is append-only and lives beside the queue's own log, so a shadow measurement can be read without asking the queue to explain itself.
